channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Lula diz que conversas com Trump são 'civilizadas e respeitosas', mas segundo escalão dos EUA 'toma atitudes impensáveis'
item.description: Lula stated that his conversations with Trump are 'civilized and respectful', but criticized the U.S. 'second tier' for taking 'unthinkable actions', such as imposing tariffs on Brazilian products. In an interview with TV Record, the president said the U.S. allegations justifying the sanctions are 'unfounded' and 'false', mentioning deforestation and slave labor. After a 1h20 phone call between the presidents, Brazil and the U.S. scheduled a meeting for next week between their trade ministers.

item.title: Kassab afirma que nunca falou de apoio a Lula em eventual 2º turno
item.description: Gilberto Kassab, leader of the PSD and vice-presidential candidate alongside Ronaldo Caiado, denied having stated support for President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in a potential runoff election. The statement came amid discussions about alliances and strategies for the 2026 elections.

item.title: Caiado chama Lula e Flávio de “fujões” após ausência em debate
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado criticized Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro's absence from the presidential debate promoted by Band, calling them 'cowards'. Romeu Zema also withdrew from participating after the PT candidate's no-show. The episode highlighted the polarization and evasion of central figures in the race.

item.title: Debate na Band: colunistas do GLOBO comentam o 1º confronto presidencial de 2026; siga ao vivo
item.description: The first 2026 presidential debate, broadcast by Band, featured GLOBO columnists analyzing the absence of Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro. Zema canceled his participation citing Lula's absence, while Flávio gave a speech in Barretos without concrete proposals for agriculture. Lula denied trying to block investigations into his son and promised punishment if wrongdoing occurred.

item.title: Lula e Flávio deveriam perder registro de candidatura por faltar ao debate, diz Caiado
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado criticized Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro's absence from the Band TV debate, stating they should lose their candidacy registration for disrespecting society. Romeu Zema also skipped the event. The former Goiás governor deemed their absence an affront to the Brazilian electorate.

item.title: Debate da Band terá púlpitos vazios para Lula, Flávio e Zema
item.description: Band TV will keep empty podiums in the studio for Lula (PT), Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), and Romeu Zema (Novo), who have already confirmed they will not attend the presidential debate this Sunday (23). The event, starting at 8 PM, will feature only Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) and Renan Santos (Mission) among the announced candidates.

item.title: Renan leva ao debate fraldas com nomes de “Flávio e Lula”
item.description: Renan Santos brought diapers labeled 'Flávio' and 'Lula' to the first presidential debate hosted by Band TV, mocking the absence of both candidates. The act highlights the lack of engagement from the main contenders in the electoral process.

item.title: Com fraldas, Renan Santos chama Lula e Flávio de “criminosos”
item.description: Renan Santos criticized the absence of Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in the first presidential debate, calling them criminals and scumbags and bringing symbolic diapers. He cited investigations like Banco Master and INSS, accusing them of organized crime dealings. Other candidates like Romeu Zema also withdrew.

item.title: Em debate da Band, Renan Santos leva fraldas para Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Renan Santos (Missão) attended the first Band presidential debate carrying diapers labeled with the names of Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), the two main absentees. He accused both of being 'criminals' linked to organized crime and of avoiding the debate out of fear.

item.title: Datafolha: para 50% dos eleitores, há chance de outros países interferirem na eleição brasileira
item.description: A Datafolha survey reveals that 50% of Brazilian voters believe other countries may interfere in the 2026 elections, with 32% viewing it as a problem and 18% not. The poll, conducted between August 18 and 19 with 2,058 respondents, has a margin of error of two percentage points and a 95% confidence level.

item.title: Lula diz que Lulinha “vai ser punido” se tiver cometido crime e critica entorno de Trump
item.description: President Lula stated that his son Lulinha will be punished if he committed any crime, taking the Federal Police investigations into influence peddling in federal contracts seriously. The probes also involve former chief of staff Marcola and lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger, suspected of buying jewelry and paying expenses to gain access to Lula's inner circle. Lula declared he does not interfere with the investigations and that 'no one is immune' if they made mistakes.

item.title: Debate presidencial: candidatos se enfrentam na Band; acompanhe
item.description: Lula will skip the presidential debate on Band and instead give an interview to Record at the same time. The candidate confirms he will maintain other media engagements, including an appearance on Globo after the national news.

item.title: Mais de 900 candidatos mudaram declaração de cor entre 2022 e 2026
item.description: A g1 analysis of TSE data shows that 909 out of 6,315 candidates who ran in both 2022 and 2026 changed their declared race or color, representing 14.4% of the sample. The most common shift was from brown to white, with 322 instances.

item.title: Veja como foi o domingo (23) dos candidatos a presidente
item.description: Three candidates participated in the first 2026 presidential debate promoted by Band TV, while others held political or religious events or had no public schedule. Zema and Marçal stood out by withdrawing from the debate and being barred from campaigning, respectively. Issues such as housing, healthcare, and education were discussed, especially by Hertz Dias.

item.title: A versão petista para afastar Lula do escândalo de Lulinha e Marcola
item.description: PT allies claim former chief of staff Marcola misused his position and Lula's name to benefit Lulinha and Roberta Luchsinger. The defense argues Marcola acted independently, leveraging the perceived power of his office to open government doors. Ongoing STF investigations must progress to clarify the facts.

item.title: Especialistas apontam fatores decisivos para eleger o novo presidente da República
item.description: Experts highlight that the economy, candidate rejection rates, and voter abstention will be decisive in the 2026 presidential election. Lula's re-election hinges on economic performance and voter mobilization, while Flávio Bolsonaro faces challenges from high rejection rates and ongoing investigations.

item.title: Lula diz tratar com 'muita seriedade' caso sobre Lulinha e afirma: 'Investigue-se'
item.description: President Lula stated that he treats with 'great seriousness' the investigations against his son Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha, and former chief of staff Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro, known as Marcola. In an interview with Record on Sunday the 23rd, the president and re-election candidate called for the case to be investigated. The statement comes amid political fallout from suspicions involving people close to the president.

item.title: STF ameaça multar partidos por omitir informações sobre emendas parlamentares
item.description: The STF gave Podemos and Solidariedade five days to clarify whether their presidents control parliamentary amendments, under threat of a daily fine of R$ 100,000. Nineteen other parties have already stated they have no such control. Justice Dino also invalidated amendments indicated by politicians not holding current elected office.

item.title: 'Volta a fita': De Brizola x Maluf a Lula x Bolsonaro, assista aos momentos marcantes dos debates na estreia da série
item.description: The first 2026 presidential debate, hosted by TV Bandeirantes, features Ronaldo Caiado, Renan Santos, and Augusto Cury, with Romeu Zema withdrawing and Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro unconfirmed. GLOBO's 'Volta a fita' series revisits historic debate moments, while its special coverage includes live analyses, newsletters, and the 'Fora da bolha' videocast.

item.title: Lulinha “tem que provar a inocência dele”, diz Lula
item.description: President Lula stated he treats the investigations involving his son, Lulinha, and former chief of staff Marcola with 'great seriousness'. He remarked that Lulinha 'must prove his innocence', indicating the government takes the process seriously.

item.title: Debate de Band e ‘Estadão’ com candidatos a presidente começa em qual horário?
item.description: The first 2026 presidential debate, hosted by Band, Estadão, TV Cultura, Gazeta and Jovem Pan, will take place this Sunday (23rd) at 8 PM (Brasília time). Augusto Cury (Avante), Renan Santos (Missão) and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) confirmed attendance; Romeu Zema (Novo) canceled, while Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) were invited but are not expected to show up. At the same time, Record TV will air an interview with Lula, who criticized Zema's and Renan Santos' inclusion in the debate.

item.title: Quais bens canadenses sofrerão as tarifas de 50% de Trump? Alguns itens são bastante estranhos
item.description: The U.S. imposed 50% tariffs on approximately $20 billion worth of Canadian exports—including waterproof jackets, national flags, Christmas decorations, and 36 types of plywood—after trade negotiations collapsed. The Trump administration frames the tariffs as retaliatory, while Canada pledges dollar-for-dollar retaliation, directly impacting its forestry industry and U.S. housing construction costs.

item.title: Lula discute investigações de Lulinha em entrevista transmitida durante debate em que vai faltar
item.description: President Lula gave an interview to Record during the same time slot as the Band debate, addressing investigations involving his son Lulinha and former chief of staff Marcola. Lula denied attempting to interfere with investigations and stated his son will face justice. He also withdrew from the debate and criticized the invitation to candidates Zema and Renan Santos.

item.title: ‘Record’ mostra entrevista exclusiva de Lula na hora do debate na ‘Band’
item.description: Record will air an exclusive interview with President Lula on Sunday, coinciding with Band's first debate of the year without his attendance. Lula defended the investigations into his son, Lulinha, and pledged not to interfere, contrasting his stance with that of his predecessor.

item.title: Sem confirmar presença em debate, Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula não têm agendas neste domingo
item.description: The polling leaders Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro did not confirm their attendance at the debate promoted by Band, keeping empty schedules this Sunday. With the absence of the two, the debate will be held only by the candidates Ronaldo Caiado, Renan Santos and Augusto Cury. Zema's decision not to participate was attributed to Lula's absence and other competitors at the event.

item.title: Lula diz que não tenta 'proibir investigação' sobre Lulinha e que, se filho errou, 'vai ser punido'
item.description: Lula stated he does not interfere in the investigations involving his son Lulinha, asserting that if wrongdoing is proven, his son will be judged and punished. He emphasized that no one is above the law and advised his son to defend himself publicly.

item.title: A conexão entre o escândalo que envolve Lulinha e a investigação de lobby da ex-nora de Lula
item.description: The Federal Police is investigating links between the lobbying scheme of Lula's former daughter-in-law, Carla Trindade, and the case involving Lulinha and Roberta Luchsinger. Both groups allegedly shared the Bittar brothers as 'partners' to operate within the government. Investigators are considering sharing evidence, including compromising messages, to build a broader influence-peddling case involving figures close to the Presidency.

item.title: Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, o deserto de ideias e o futuro negado ao Brasil
item.description: Political polarization is preventing substantive debate, turning the 2026 election into an 'ideas desert'. Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro focus on mutual rejection and undermining each other rather than presenting detailed plans for chronic issues like public security and public finances. Both candidates prefer betting on the other's rejection than on a vision for Brazil's future.

item.title: Durigan vira porta-voz de Lula em ofensiva contra Flávio na economia
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan has become Lula's main spokesperson defending the government's economic policy, directly attacking Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL-RJ) presidential campaign proposals as 'baloney' (nonsense). Durigan also attributed part of inflationary pressure to wars supported by bolsonarismo and labeled the Bolsonaro administration as 'regulatory anarchy'. As a trusted figure of Lula and former minister Haddad, Durigan signals possible directions for a potential fourth Lula term starting in 2026.

item.title: Quem ganha e quem perde com a entrada de Pablo Marçal na disputa presidencial
item.description: Pablo Marçal (PRTB) filed his presidential candidacy on Aug 15, 2026, but remains ineligible until 2032 per an Electoral Court ruling. The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) barred him from public campaign funds and participation in debates/TV-radio ads. Analysts say his entry could shake up a polarized race between Lula (PT, 39%) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL, 35%), mainly by competing for right-wing voters seeking alternatives.

item.title: Kataguiri chama Zema de “arregão” após desistência de debate
item.description: Federal deputy Kim Kataguiri (Missão-SP) called Romeu Zema (Novo) a coward ("arregão") after the former governor of Minas Gerais withdrew from the Band presidential debate scheduled for Sunday. Zema's decision came after the confirmed absences of Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) from the event.

item.title: Lula de chapéu na urna: Ministério Público Eleitoral defende liberar foto de presidente com acessório
item.description: Brazil's Electoral Public Ministry (MPE) told the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) that it sees no irregularity in Lula's ballot photo featuring a hat, arguing the attire aligns with political pluralism. The hat has been worn by the president for medical reasons following skin cancer surgery. Deputy Electoral Prosecutor-General Alexandre Espinosa stated the clothing does not hinder voter recognition, citing a 2022 TSE precedent that allowed PT deputy Douglas Belchior to wear a cap on his ballot.

item.title: PÚBLICO da FESTA do PEÃO de BARRETOS recebe FLÁVIO e XINGA LULA ao VIVO na GLOBO
item.description: The crowd at Festa do Peão de Barretos booed President Lula during a live broadcast by Globo, while Flávio Bolsonaro was welcomed with applause. The incident sparked strong public reaction and became a highlight of the festival's coverage.

item.title: Tema central da eleição, Lulinha reaviva rixa entre advogado e chefe do PT
item.description: Investigations into Lulinha's alleged influence peddling reignited rivalry between lawyer Marco Aurélio de Carvalho and PT leader Edinho Silva. Marco Aurélio became the main defender of Lula and his son against accusations from Flávio Bolsonaro and Alfredo Gaspar, countering that opponents use politically instrumentalized Federal Police sectors because they lack votes and a government program.

item.title: Tarcísio diz que "pode mais" e pede novo "voto de confiança" em SP
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans), running for reelection, asked voters for a new 'vote of confidence' at the launch of Renata Abreu's (Podemos) candidacy for the Chamber of Deputies. He highlighted his administration's achievements and defended expanding TEA Centers for mothers of autistic children, while also endorsing Senate candidates and Mayor Ricardo Nunes (MDB). The campaign strategy prioritizes female voters.

item.title: Eleitores participam de eleição simulada no Maranhão
item.description: Voters in Paulino Neves, Maranhão, participated in a TSE-simulated election to test systems for the 2026 General Elections. The simulation involved 1,398 volunteers (9.22% of the electorate), 24 polling stations, and training of poll workers, with no reported issues.

item.title: Zema desiste de participar do debate na ‘Band’
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) withdrew from the Band TV debate just hours before its scheduled start on Sunday. Lula's (PT) expected absence, which prompted the change, joins Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) likely no-show, leaving the event with only Caiado (PSD), Renan Santos (Mission) and Augusto Cury (Avante).

item.title: Romeu Zema desiste de debate presidencial da Band devido à ‘ausência de Lula e outros concorrentes’
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) dropped out of the Bandeirantes presidential debate scheduled for this Sunday (23), joining the earlier withdrawals of Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). His campaign argued the date was moved to accommodate Lula, so without him and other rivals the debate lost its purpose. The event is now expected to feature only Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), Renan Santos (Missão) and Augusto Cury (Avante), with three thematic blocks starting at 8 p.m. (Brasília time).

item.title: Sem Lula, Flávio e Zema, Caiado diz que vai a debate: "Não dou marcha ré"
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) confirmed he will attend the first 2026 presidential debate on Sunday (Aug 13) on Band, stating he 'doesn't back down.' The event will feature only three candidates—Caiado, Augusto Cury (Avante), and Renan Santos (Missão)—after the absences of Lula (PT), Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), and Romeu Zema (Novo), the latter declining due to the absence of the leading frontrunners.

item.title: Para adversários, Zema desistiu de candidatura ao não ir a debate
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) skipped the Band debate, which rivals interpreted as a withdrawal due to low poll numbers. Zema's campaign argues the debate lost relevance without Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro. He will compensate with an interview on Jornal Nacional.

item.title: Advogado herda número de Marçal e se lança candidato pelo União Brasil
item.description: Lawyer Tassio Renam, Pablo Marçal's ally, was registered by União Brasil as a federal deputy candidate inheriting number 4444. Marçal returned to PRTB to run for President but remains ineligible for 8 years. The party's strategy is to transfer Marçal's voter base, which nearly reached São Paulo's 2024 runoff, to his former right-hand man.

item.title: Marcola pode virar um novo ‘Mauro Cid’? No Planalto, muita gente está preocupada
item.description: VEJA magazine revealed that lobbyist Roberta Luchsinger paid personal expenses of Marco Aurélio Santana Ribeiro, known as Marcola, former chief of staff to Lula, in a scheme investigated by the Federal Police. Despite the revelations, Lula defends the former aide, but there are concerns at the Presidential Palace that he could become a 'new Mauro Cid' if abandoned.

item.title: Planos de candidatos à Presidência têm de 7 a 200 páginas
item.description: The 2026 presidential campaign plans range from 7 to 200 pages, with no clear correlation between length and detail. Augusto Cury (Avante) leads with 200 pages, while Rui Costa Pimenta (PCO) has the shortest at 7 pages. Documents include proposals, financial simulations, and action schedules, reflecting varied strategic approaches.

item.title: Lula estuda medida de duplo alcance eleitoral
item.description: Lula announces a 200+ billion reais package to boost popularity and re-election bid, but remains in a technical tie with Flávio Bolsonaro in runoff polls. The president considers raising Bolsa Família payments before October to address cost-of-living complaints and reduce abstention among low-income voters — his core base — mirroring Bolsonaro's 2022 strategy.

item.title: MPE libera foto de Lula com chapéu na urna eletrônica
item.description: Brazil's Electoral Prosecutor's Office (MPE) defended before the TSE the validation of Lula's photo for the electronic ballot, in which the president appears wearing a hat on medical recommendation after the removal of a skin cancer lesion. The Deputy Prosecutor-General stated that the accessory does not constitute campaign propaganda nor hinders the candidate's identification, serving political pluralism. The choice divided experts, as the item is not part of the PT politician's historical visual identification.

item.title: Que horas é o debate presidencial? Band promove primeiro debate neste domingo; veja como assistir
item.description: The first open-TV presidential debate will air on Band at 8 PM this Sunday. Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro have not confirmed attendance, and Romeu Zema withdrew. The debate will feature Augusto Cury, Renan Santos, and Ronaldo Caiado.

item.title: Lula dá entrevista à Record e fala sobre Lulinha, Marcola e Trump
item.description: President Lula gave an interview to TV Record at the Alvorada Palace, addressing investigations involving his son Lulinha and former chief of staff Marcola, reiterating that anyone who committed irregularities must answer for their actions. He also discussed his phone call with US President Donald Trump and topics such as public security and education. The interview, conducted by journalist Mariana Godoy, was scheduled to air on Sunday night.

item.title: Renan Santos confirma presença em debate e critica “descompromisso” de candidatos
item.description: Presidential candidate Renan Santos (Missão) confirmed his participation in the Band debate on Sunday, 23rd, despite Romeu Zema's (Novo) withdrawal. He strongly criticized the absence of other candidates, calling it a 'shame' and 'lack of commitment'.

item.title: Lula vai ao debate hoje? Veja quem deve participar do encontro na Band
item.description: The first 2026 presidential debate is scheduled for today on Band, but it will not feature the two frontrunners in the race for the Planalto Palace: President Lula (PT) and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). The absence of the polling leaders raises questions about the format and relevance of the event for voters.

item.title: Zema cancela participação no debate eleitoral promovido por Band e Estadão
item.description: Romeu Zema, presidential candidate for the Novo Party, withdrew from the electoral debate hosted by Band and Estadão, scheduled for today at 8 PM. The event is co-hosted by TV Cultura, Gazeta, and Jovem Pan. The reason for his absence was not disclosed.
